allDirectChanges.before:
Creates a reusable email design and publishes it as version 1, so a transactional send can use it at once by its `id` or `alias`. An agent key's template stays a draft until a person publishes it.

`transactionalDefaults` holds the subject, preview text and sender that a **transactional send** of this template uses unless the send gives its own, so a subject change needs no deploy. Campaigns and journeys copy the design when they pick the template and set their own subject and sender; later edits to the template don't change them.

Each use checks what it needs: campaigns and journeys refuse raw HTML blocks, and marketing email gets its unsubscribe link and postal address added at send time.

With an `alias`, a retry after the first call succeeded is refused with 409 `ALREADY_EXISTS`: the first call created it. Without one, send an `Idempotency-Key`.

Requires API-key scope: `templates:write`.
allDirectChanges.after:
Creates a reusable email and publishes it as version 1, so a transactional send can use it at once by its `id` or `alias`. An agent key's template stays a draft until a person publishes it.

`transactionalDefaults` holds the subject, preview text and sender that a **transactional send** of this template uses unless the send gives its own, so a subject change needs no deploy. Campaigns and journeys copy the design when they pick the template and set their own subject and sender; later edits to the template don't change them.

A template is one of two kinds, fixed when it is created. A `design` (the default) is built from blocks. An `html` template holds the whole email as `html`, kept as code: saving removes scripts, event handlers, frames, forms, SVG, `javascript:` links and stylesheet links other than Google Fonts (email apps drop them anyway), and keeps the rest as written, Outlook conditional comments included. CSS is not inlined. `POST /v1/templates/render` lists what saving would remove.

Each use checks what it needs: campaigns and journeys refuse raw HTML blocks in a design, and marketing email gets an unsubscribe link and the postal address added at send time unless the email already shows them; in HTML, `{{unsubscribe_url}}` as a link's href places the link.

With an `alias`, a retry after the first call succeeded is refused with 409 `ALREADY_EXISTS`: the first call created it. Without one, send an `Idempotency-Key`.

Requires API-key scope: `templates:write`.

allDirectChanges.before:
Renders a saved template to the subject, HTML and plain text a recipient would get, without sending or changing anything. A template never published is 409 `TEMPLATE_NOT_PUBLISHED` for `published`. allDirectChanges.before:

Merge tags show their defaults, or pass `contact` to render them as that contact would see them (not from an embed session). `warnings` flags problems that do not stop rendering, such as an oversized message, or `POSTAL_ADDRESS_MISSING` while the workspace has no `postalAddress` for the footer.

allDirectChanges.after:
Renders a block tree and theme sent in the request, or an email written as HTML (`"kind": "html"`), to the HTML and plain text a recipient would get, without saving anything: the builder or code editor preview, plain-text view and HTML export. HTML is returned as saving would keep it, with `HTML_REMOVED` listing what saving removes, `UNSUBSCRIBE_LINK_ADDED` when no link goes to `{{unsubscribe_url}}`, `UNUSABLE_ADDRESS` naming empty, `#` or relative link and image addresses, and `PLACEHOLDER_LINK` naming placeholder addresses (example.com and the like), which sending refuses as it does in a design. With `"context": "marketing"` the HTML shows the postal address and unsubscribe link a marketing send adds when the email lacks them; `"transactional"`, the default, adds nothing and returns the HTML as saving keeps it. To render a saved template, use `POST /v1/templates/{id}/render`. Merge tags show their defaults, or pass `contact` to render them as that contact would see them (not from an embed session). `warnings` flags problems that do not stop rendering, such as an oversized message, or `POSTAL_ADDRESS_MISSING` while the workspace has no `postalAddress` for the footer.

Requires API-key scope: `templates:read`.

allDirectChanges.before:
Sends the design in the request to one workspace member who has accepted their invitation; call once per recipient. Pass `contact` to render merge tags as that contact would see them. The test comes from `from`, or the workspace's default sender, on a verified sending domain: there is no shared sender, so a workspace sends tests once its own domain is verified (`SENDING_DOMAIN_UNVERIFIED` before then). An embed session may call this too: a session lets the chosen builders read what they need, render previews, count audiences, upload images and, when `testSendTo` lists addresses, send test emails to those addresses only. allDirectChanges.before:
Sends a one-off message to one recipient — a receipt, a password reset, a confirmation — bypassing campaigns. It ignores marketing preferences (it is the critical tier) but respects suppression. Agent keys are refused with 403.

**Channels.** Give `email`, `push`, or both. With both, `deliver: "all"` (the default) sends each one the contact can receive. `deliver: { "first": ["email", "push"] }` tries them in that order: the first the contact can receive goes, and each later one waits as a fallback (`fallbackFor`), sent only when the one before it fails, is skipped or bounces (an email gets 15 minutes to bounce), else skipped with reason `fallback_not_needed`. A fallback is charged only when it goes; with no room left in the plan by then it is skipped with reason `plan_limit_reached`. A channel the contact cannot receive, or the plan has no room for, is passed over and listed in `skippedChannels` with its error code; only when none is left does the send fail, with that channel's error. So with `all` too, a 202 can leave a channel unsent: check `skippedChannels`. The response lists one message per channel stored.

**Data.** `data` holds the values the content reads as `{{ data.<key> }}`, once for every channel: a stored template, inline email, and the push `title` and `body`. Inline content (email or push) whose `{{ data.<key> }}` tag has no value in `data`, and no default, is refused with 400 rather than sent blank.

**Email.** Inline (`subject`, `from`, `html`, optional `text`, `previewText`, `replyTo`), or a stored template named by `template` (its alias, such as `password-reset`, or its id). The template's published version is rendered when the request is accepted and supplies the envelope; each envelope field given overrides it. The result needs a `subject` and a `from` (409 `TEMPLATE_ENVELOPE_INCOMPLETE`), and the `from` domain must be verified. A template never published is 409 `TEMPLATE_NOT_PUBLISHED`. Email is tracked only when `tracking` asks, and never for a contact in the EEA or the UK; `threading` continues a conversation. `attachments`, `threading` and `tracking` sit inside `email`.

**Push.** `push` takes the notification fields (`title`, `body`, `actionUrl`, …) beside `pushProjectId`, which is needed only when the workspace has several push projects. Unlike email, push needs the contact's push consent (`consent.push`) besides a device that allows notifications.

**Recipient.** `to` names one `contactId`, `externalId` or `email`, and nothing else: set a contact's name or attributes with `POST /v1/contacts/identify` first. An `email` that matches no contact creates one for transactional mail only.

**Retries.** Send an `Idempotency-Key` header to make a retry safe. A retry with the same key and request returns the first result, with `Idempotency-Replay: true`, and sends nothing again; the same key with a different request is 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`. Without a key, every request sends: a retry after a timeout can send the message twice. A replay answers from the messages as they are now, so its `status` can differ from the first answer, and an `externalId` or `email` recipient the first request created or updated stays so even when the send itself was refused. Set `correlationId` to your own reference: it is echoed on each message's webhooks and its read, and `GET /v1/messages?correlationId=` finds them. `sendAt` times the send, email and push alike.

Requires API-key scope: `transactional:send`.

allDirectChanges.before:
Edits the template's draft. Campaigns and journeys that already copied it keep the content they were built with, and transactional sends keep the published version until `POST /v1/templates/{id}/publish`. `transactionalDefaults` is part of the draft and is published with it: a field left out stays as it is, and `null` clears it.

context.description: HTML only. `marketing`: the email as a marketing send has it, with the postal address and an unsubscribe link (`{{unsubscribe_url}}`; `#` in a test send) added below when the HTML does not show them. `transactional` (the default): nothing is added, as a transactional send adds nothing, and the HTML is as saving keeps it.

plainTextOverride.description: Plain text used instead of the version generated from the design or HTML.

contact.description: A contact whose values fill the merge tags and decide each block's `visibleIf`. Without one, merge tags show their defaults.

data.description: Sample data for `{{ event.properties.* }}` tags and repeat lists: what a transactional send's `data` or a journey's event would carry. Without it, a repeat shows once with its item tags as written.

from.description: The address the test comes from, on one of the workspace's verified domains; the workspace's default sender when omitted.

to.description: Where to send the test: any member of the workspace who has accepted their invitation.

subscribed.description: Join (true) or leave (false) the topic on every channel; it clears each channel's own choice.

channels.description: One channel's choice each, applied after `subscribed`; a channel left out keeps its choice.

first.description: Every channel given, each once, in the order to try them. The first the contact can receive is sent; when sending it fails, it is skipped or it bounces, the next is sent.

anyOf.description: Every channel given that the contact can receive.

The contact column to test. Each takes these operators, and is refused with others: `email`: equals, notEquals, contains, startsWith, exists, notExists, in; `firstName`: equals, notEquals, contains, startsWith, exists, notExists, in; `lastName`: equals, notEquals, contains, startsWith, exists, notExists, in; `phone`: equals, notEquals, contains, startsWith, exists, notExists, in; `timezone`: equals, notEquals, contains, startsWith, exists, notExists, in; `externalId`: equals, notEquals, contains, startsWith, exists, notExists, in; `consent.email`: equals; `consent.push`: equals; `country`: equals, notEquals, in, exists, notExists; `locale`: equals, notEquals, startsWith, in, exists, notExists; `rfmGroup`: equals, notEquals, in, exists, notExists; `rfmRecency`: equals, notEquals, in, exists, notExists, gt, gte, lt, lte; `rfmFrequency`: equals, notEquals, in, exists, notExists, gt, gte, lt, lte; `rfmMonetary`: equals, notEquals, in, exists, notExists, gt, gte, lt, lte; `purchaseCount`: equals, gt, gte, lt, lte; `totalSpent`: equals, gt, gte, lt, lte; `lastPurchasedAt`: before, after, withinLastDays, moreThanDaysAgo, exists, notExists; `createdAt`: before, after, withinLastDays, moreThanDaysAgo. `phone` holds +country numbers: write `equals`, `notEquals` and `in` values with their country code. Consent takes `true` or `false`.

Purchases: `purchaseCount`, `totalSpent` (in the main currency) and `lastPurchasedAt` are a customer's totals of the workspace's purchase event (`purchaseEvent` in workspace settings: an order, a paid invoice, a booking), recomputed daily; the contact's stored `totalSpent` is null when the workspace's purchases carry no amount. In comparisons on `purchaseCount` and `totalSpent` a missing count or spend is 0, so someone who never purchased has 0 purchases and 0 spent.

RFM: `rfmGroup` and its scores `rfmRecency`, `rfmFrequency` and `rfmMonetary` (monetary value: how much they spend) come from the same daily pass. A score is a whole number from 1 to 5 (an array of them for `in`), 5 being the most recent, most frequent or highest spending; any other value is refused with 400. Someone who never purchased has no `rfmGroup` or scores: on those four fields they match only `notExists` and `notEquals`. So `rfmRecency` `notEquals` 5 includes everyone who never purchased; add an `exists` rule on the same field to leave them out (bought, but not recently).
